How we work

What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 01

    1–2 weeks

    Discover

    We walk the patient journey with front office, nursing, lab and pharmacy staff, on site or by video, map where calls and delays pile up, and review what the HIS, LIS or POS can expose. We also review current consent forms, the privacy notice and existing messaging practices.

    Deliverables

    • Journey map with failure points for each segment you operate
    • Systems and data inventory with integration options
    • Consent, channel and platform policy gap review
    • Prioritized automation backlog with effort ranges

    What we need from you

    • HIS, LIS or POS administrator and API documentation or vendor contact
    • Current consent forms, privacy notice and message templates
    • Anonymized hourly volumes for calls, bookings and reports
    • Named owners: medical superintendent or lab director, IT head, front-office lead
  2. 02

    1–2 weeks

    Design

    We design conversation flows, templates, routing rules and data flows, including the emergency and symptom handling script. Clinical content and consent wording are written or approved by your team, not by us.

    Deliverables

    • Conversation flows and template drafts for WhatsApp approval and DLT registration
    • Emergency and symptom routing rules for clinical sign-off
    • Data flow diagram with retention and access for each field
    • Owner and escalation matrix

    What we need from you

    • Clinical sign-off on routing rules by the medical superintendent, lab director or pharmacist in charge
    • Consent and notice wording reviewed by your legal or compliance owner
    • WhatsApp Business account, display name and DLT entity registration access
  3. 03

    2–4 weeks

    Build

    We build the integrations in n8n and the agreed tools against a test environment with synthetic or de-identified data, set up the consent log, staff queues and dashboards, and document every connection and credential owner.

    Deliverables

    • Working integrations in a test environment
    • Consent and purpose log
    • Staff queues and dashboards
    • Integration documentation and access list

    What we need from you

    • Sandbox or test access to the HIS, LIS or POS
    • De-identified sample reports and documents for testing
    • Staff time for weekly build reviews
  4. 04

    1–2 weeks

    Validate & launch

    We test with front-office staff, nurses and pharmacists, run a scripted set of symptom, emergency and edge-case messages, fix what fails and launch in one department, unit or branch before any wider rollout.

    Deliverables

    • Test report including safety script results
    • Go-live checklist and rollback plan
    • Staff training and quick reference guides
    • Operating runbook

    What we need from you

    • Go-live approval from the medical superintendent and the data protection contact
    • Staff available for training and the first live week
  5. 05

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    Operate & improve

    We monitor failed messages, template quality ratings, handoffs and model accuracy, review KPIs with your owners each month, and change content and rules only through a controlled, approved change process.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly KPI and quality review
    • Failure and incident log with fixes
    • Quarterly access and retention review
    • Change log for templates, rules and prompts

    What we need from you

    • Named owner for change approvals
    • Monthly review time with operations and clinical leads

Suggested first pilot

Five-week OPD booking and reminder pilot

Start with one OPD department or doctor group. The first two weeks connect its slots, get templates approved and run the safety script; for three live weeks patients book, confirm and reschedule on WhatsApp while every symptom or complaint reaches a staffed queue. We compare no-shows and response times with the weeks before, using your own HIS data.

  • One OPD department or doctor group on the hospital's verified WhatsApp Business number
  • Booking, confirmation, reminder and reschedule templates approved by Meta and your clinical lead
  • Emergency and symptom routing to a named, staffed queue during agreed hours
  • Consent log and a daily report of failed or unanswered messages
  • Baseline and pilot comparison of no-shows and first response time

Governance

Safe by design, owned by your team.

  • Consent first: every message type is tied to a recorded opt-in and notice version, and withdrawal on any channel stops automated messages for that purpose.
  • No clinical decisions by software: AI may classify, extract and summarize, but diagnosis, triage, result interpretation, prescribing and dispensing stay with qualified staff.
  • Safety testing on every change: a symptom and emergency test script approved by the clinical lead runs before each release of templates, rules or prompts.
  • Minimum data in messages: notifications carry no diagnosis, test values or medicine names, and documents open only behind verified, expiring links.
  • Role-based access, processing logs kept for at least one year as the DPDP Rules require, quarterly access reviews, and AI providers used under enterprise terms without training on patient data.
  • An incident and breach runbook that supports the DPDP duty to inform affected patients and the Data Protection Board without delay, with a detailed report to the Board within seventy-two hours.

Compliance notes

The obligations that shape the design.

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025

Health data is personal data under the DPDP Act. Most duties in the Rules notified on 13 November 2025 apply eighteen months later, and we design for them now: standalone notices, security safeguards with logs kept for at least a year, breach intimation to patients and the Board without delay and a detailed Board report within seventy-two hours, and verifiable parental consent for children, with a limited exemption for health providers treating a child.

meity.gov.in · Source ↗

Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and ABHA

Where a facility uses ABDM-enabled software, records are linked to the patient's ABHA and exchanged only with the patient's revocable, time-bound consent, under the National Health Authority's Health Data Management Policy. Our automations prompt and track optional ABHA linking and Scan and Share registration, and leave the consented exchange itself to the ABDM-integrated HIS or LIS.

pib.gov.in · Source ↗

Clinical Establishments Act 2010 and state equivalents

Establishments register under the central Act where a state or union territory has adopted it, or under state law. The central rules require rates for each service displayed in the local language and English and records kept as governments prescribe, and the Act requires care to stabilize emergencies within available means. Quoted prices must match the rate card, and clinically relevant messages flow back into the facility's records.

clinicalestablishments.mohfw.gov.in · Source ↗

Medical ethics: solicitation, advertising and referral fees

In August 2023 the NMC held its 2023 professional conduct regulations in abeyance and applied the 2002 Code of Ethics Regulations; we confirm the current position with your compliance owner before launch. The 2002 code treats soliciting patients by physicians or institutions as unethical, bars self-advertisement and boasting of cures, and prohibits referral commissions and fee-splitting. Package messages stay factual, with no testimonials or cure claims.

nmc.org.in · Source ↗

Prescription medicines under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules

Schedule H, H1 and X medicines may be sold by retail only on a registered medical practitioner's prescription, dispensed by or under a registered pharmacist, and H1 supplies need a separate register kept for three years. Our pharmacy workflows put every prescription before a pharmacist, prompt the H1 register entry, never suggest substitutes, fill remote orders only from licensed premises and never confirm Schedule X orders remotely.

pib.gov.in · Source ↗

WhatsApp policy and TRAI rules for patient messaging

WhatsApp requires opt-in before a business messages a patient, approved templates outside the 24-hour customer service window and a clear route to a person, and prohibits using it to buy, sell or promote prescription drugs. SMS and calls in India follow TRAI's TCCCPR: registered DLT headers and templates, recorded consent and DND preferences, and promotional content inside a service message makes it promotional.

business.whatsapp.com · Source ↗

Questions

Frequently asked.

Will an AI chatbot give medical advice to our patients?

No. The automation answers administrative questions such as timings, fees, preparation and directions from content your team approves. Messages that describe symptoms or ask about medicines or results go to a nurse, doctor or pharmacist, and emergency words trigger an immediate instruction to call your emergency number or 112. Your clinical lead signs off the routing rules and the safety test script before launch.

Do we need to replace our HIS, LIS or pharmacy software?

No. We connect to the systems you already run through their APIs, HL7 or FHIR interfaces, vendor integrations or approved exports. Where a system offers no interface, we agree a safe interim route such as scheduled exports and state its limits clearly. Your HIS, LIS or POS remains the source of truth.

Is it safe to send lab reports and discharge summaries on WhatsApp?

We send a notification on WhatsApp, not the clinical content. The patient opens the report or summary through a secure, expiring link after entering a one-time code sent to their registered mobile number, and every open is logged. Health data stays in systems you control, which supports the security safeguards the DPDP Act expects.

Can our pharmacy take medicine orders on WhatsApp?

WhatsApp's business messaging policy prohibits using the platform to buy, sell or promote prescription drugs and restricts other healthcare product messaging. We therefore build ordering and refill reminders on the pharmacy's own app, website, counter, SMS and email, and a registered pharmacist verifies every prescription.

How does this work with ABDM and ABHA?

If your facility uses ABDM-enabled software, we prompt patients about optional ABHA linking, support Scan and Share at registration and give staff a view of linking status. The consented exchange of records itself runs through your ABDM-integrated HIS or LIS and the ABDM consent manager, not through our workflows.

How long does a first project take, and what drives the cost?

A first pilot usually runs three to six weeks, depending mainly on HIS access and template approvals. We quote after discovery, once your systems, volumes and existing tool licenses are known. Provider charges, such as WhatsApp template message fees, SMS and model usage, are billed by those providers and shown separately.

We also treat patients from abroad. Does that change anything?

It can. If you offer services to people in the EU, the GDPR may apply alongside the DPDP Act, and US partners may ask for HIPAA-style business associate terms before sharing health information. We scope these requirements with your legal team during discovery; nothing on this page is legal advice.

Who owns the patient conversations and data?

Your facility does. We set up messaging, database and automation accounts in your organization's name wherever the provider allows it, limit our access to named people for named tasks, and hand over credentials, documentation and workflows at the end of the engagement.
